summary: workouts_list's user_id parameter is no longer required. When a caller omits it, mcpParamBinding.ResolveFromLiveProfile triggers a live GET /api/me lookup (the same endpoint account_show uses, which needs no user_id itself) via resolveLiveProfileID/resolveLiveProfileBindings, and the returned profile id is injected into the call's args before the normal path-substitution logic runs -- so every other binding-handling path treats it exactly as if the caller had supplied it directly. resolveLiveProfileID memoizes a successful lookup in a process-lifetime cache (liveProfileIDCache, mutex-guarded) -- the authenticated profile's id doesn't change within a server process's lifetime, so a fresh lookup on every omitted-user_id call would otherwise double the request volume of the most-walked endpoint (confirmed live: 75 extra round-trips for one full workouts enumeration at the default page size). A failed lookup is never cached, so a transient auth/network hiccup doesn't permanently poison every later call. A regen touching workouts_list's registration or the shared makeAPIHandlerVerbose pipeline must keep resolveLiveProfileBindings wired in before the main bindings loop reads args, and must keep the memoization (or replace it with an equivalent one) rather than reverting to a lookup-per-call.
reason: A connector-availability debugging session flagged this as an ergonomics gap: account_show already returns the authenticated profile's id, but workouts_list required a caller to already know (or separately fetch) that same id before it could page its own workout history -- a two-hop call an agent has no way to anticipate from workouts_list's schema alone. The tool description itself already flagged this as deferred work ("user_id is supplied by the caller until U3 links the profile fact"). Chose the live-lookup approach over a cheaper PELOTON_USER_ID env-var default because the env var is optional/not guaranteed to be configured (confirmed unset in at least one real deployment), while a live lookup works universally regardless of setup. Live validation (B14) then raised the memoization question directly -- confirmed unresolved from the code (no caching in the first version), and added it before the enumeration path (sync/workflow_archive) could be exercised uncached.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test (including -race on internal/mcp specifically) and verify_skill.py all green. Live-tested (B14): no user_id resolves and returns real workout data; explicit user_id produces a byte-identical response to the resolved path; a garbage user_id surfaces a genuine provider 400 with the literal value echoed in the upstream path (confirms the fallback never silently substitutes the resolved profile for an explicitly-wrong value); account_show/classes_search unaffected. New tests: TestResolveLiveProfileIDFetchesFromAPIMe, TestResolveLiveProfileIDSurfacesMissingID, TestResolveLiveProfileBindingsInjectsMissingUserID, TestResolveLiveProfileBindingsRespectsExplicitValue (zero lookup requests when the caller supplies user_id explicitly), TestResolveLiveProfileBindingsSurfacesLookupFailure, TestResolveLiveProfileIDIsMemoizedAcrossCalls (exactly one request across 3 resolutions), TestResolveLiveProfileIDDoesNotCacheFailure (a failed lookup doesn't poison the next one).
